flows.name: Nrg PV
flows.description: Generation injected into the site bus, kW.

flows.name: Nrg load
flows.description: Site demand drawn from the bus, kW.

flows.name: Nrg EV plug-in
flows.description: Energy need arriving with the vehicles that plug in, kWh/h: presence / dwell is the arrival rate, and each arrival brings its session's need.

flows.name: Nrg EV charging
flows.description: Power actually delivered to the vehicles, kW. The level being empty is what stops it asking for more than is owed.
flows.rate: min(min(TS(presence_profile), chargers) * power_per_charger_kw, (site_limit_kw if site_limit_kw > 0 else 1e9)) * (dispatch == "uncontrolled") + (dispatch == "smart") * min(min(min(TS(presence_profile), chargers) * power_per_charger_kw, (site_limit_kw if site_limit_kw > 0 else 1e9)), max((TS(price_profile) < charge_below_price) * 1e9, max(FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("demand", merit), 0)))

flows.name: Nrg EV unserved
flows.description: Energy leaving with the vehicles that unplug before they are full, kWh/h: the outstanding need divided by the mean dwell.

flows.name: Nrg Heat demand
flows.description: The site's heat demand on the heat bus, kW thermal.

flows.name: Nrg Heat from heater
flows.description: Heat made by the heat pump or heater, kW thermal. A full tank refuses it, which is what stops the heater drawing power.
flows.rate: (TS(cop_profile) if cop_profile != "" else cop) * (heater_kw * ((dispatch == "always") + (dispatch == "cheap_hours") * (TS(price_profile) < charge_below_price)) + (dispatch == "pv_surplus") * min(heater_kw, max(FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("demand", merit), 0)))

flows.name: Nrg Heat from surplus
flows.description: Heat the site would otherwise waste, taken off the heat bus at the tank's own merit so it never competes with the demand.

flows.name: Nrg Heater power
flows.description: Electricity the heater actually drew, kW: the heat it managed to put in the tank divided by the COP.
flows.rate: FLOW("$Nrg Heat from heater") / (TS(cop_profile) if cop_profile != "" else cop)

flows.name: Nrg Heat served
flows.description: Heat the tank delivered, kW thermal: what the demand still wants after every supply ahead of it. An empty tank serves less, which is exactly the unmet heat below.

flows.name: Nrg Heat standing loss
flows.description: Constant loss from the tank, kW thermal.

flows.name: Nrg Heat unmet
flows.description: Heat bought in because the tank could not cover the demand, kW thermal. It closes the heat balance and carries the bought price.

flows.name: Nrg import
flows.description: Whatever the site could not cover itself, up to the connection limit, kW.
flows.rate: min(max(FLOWSUM("demand") + FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("storage_out") - FLOWSUM("dispatchable"), 0), import_limit_kw)

flows.name: Nrg unserved
flows.description: Demand the connection limit could not deliver, kW.
flows.rate: max(FLOWSUM("demand") + FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOWSUM("generation") - FLOWSUM("storage_out") - FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOW("$Nrg import"), 0)

flows.name: Nrg export
flows.description: Surplus sold to the grid, up to the export limit, kW. A negative price is revenue.
flows.rate: min(max(FLOWSUM("generation") + FLOWSUM("storage_out") + FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("storage_in"), 0), export_limit_kw)

flows.name: Nrg curtailed
flows.description: Generation that was neither used, stored nor exported, kW.
flows.rate: max(FLOWSUM("generation") + FLOWSUM("storage_out") + FLOWSUM("dispatchable") - FLOWSUM("demand") - FLOWSUM("storage_in") - FLOW("$Nrg export"), 0)

fixed_costs.description: Capital cost of the array, annualised and prorated over the run.

info.description: Non-dispatchable generation from a normalised profile: output = profile x installed capacity x performance ratio. The profile is one value per hour of the day, in kW per kW installed, so the same asset is a wind turbine or a run-of-river plant with a different profile. Its output joins the site bus under the tag "generation", which every dispatchable asset reads -- place two arrays with different profiles and they simply add up. The annualised capital cost is a FIXED cost, prorated over the run, so a sizing run over installed_kwp compares like with like. No ports: this is a continuous asset, nothing flows through it.

parameters.name: installed_kwp
parameters.label: Installed capacity
parameters.help: Peak DC capacity. The profile is per kW installed, so this is the multiplier.

parameters.name: profile
parameters.label: Output profile
parameters.help: Normalised output, kW per kW installed, by hour of the day. Edit the values in the model's Time series tab, or import a measured year from CSV.

parameters.name: performance_ratio
parameters.label: Performance ratio
parameters.help: Everything between the panel rating and the meter: soiling, temperature, inverter and cable losses.

parameters.name: capex_per_kwp
parameters.label: Capital cost
parameters.help: Installed cost per kWp. Charged into Total Cost as a fixed cost (see the annual cost rate), so a sizing run trades it against the energy it saves.

parameters.name: annual_cost_rate
parameters.label: Annual cost rate
parameters.help: Fraction of the capital cost charged per year -- depreciation plus cost of capital. The charge is PRORATED over the run: amount x HORIZON / 8760, so a one-week run pays one week of it and capex and operating cost cover the same window. 0 leaves the capital cost out of Total Cost entirely. The model's time unit must be hours.

info.description: A depot or car park of chargers, modelled as ONE virtual battery rather than one entity per session: the presence profile says how many vehicles are plugged in each hour, each arriving vehicle brings its session's energy need, and the level holds the energy still owed to the vehicles connected right now. "uncontrolled" charges at whatever power the connected vehicles and the site cap allow; "smart" charges at full power while the price is below the threshold and otherwise only on the site's PV surplus, which is what shifting inside the dwell window costs and saves. Energy a vehicle does not get before it leaves is reported as unserved. It joins the site bus as "demand", so the Grid connection prices it with every other load and the peak it causes is its flow's Peak Rate. Limits: the aggregate is a FLEET AVERAGE -- it spreads a session's draw over the dwell instead of charging each car flat out on arrival, so the peak is honest for a carpark and optimistic for three cars; and departures take their unmet need away at the mean-dwell rate, which is exact for an exponential dwell and an approximation otherwise. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

info.description: A hot-water tank on the site's HEAT bus, in kWh thermal. It is charged by a heat pump or an electric heater -- which draws its electricity from the same site bus as every other load, divided by the COP -- and, if you give it a surplus limit, by heat the site is otherwise wasting (the Biogas library's CHP posts exactly that as "heat_supply"). It discharges against the heat demand, and whatever the tank cannot cover is bought in and reported as unmet heat. Dispatch: charge always (a thermostat), only while power is cheap, or only on the site's PV surplus -- which is what a power-to-heat case is. The standing loss is a CONSTANT kW, because a loss proportional to the content would make the tank's trajectory exponential and break the engine's exact crossings: set it to the tank's average loss, e.g. a 500 kWh tank losing 2 % of a 60 % mean fill a day is 500 x 0.6 x 0.02 / 24 = 0.25 kW. No ports: this is a continuous asset.

parameters.name: cop

parameters.name: cop_profile

info.description: The meter: whatever the site cannot cover itself is imported and priced on a tariff profile, whatever it cannot use or store is exported up to the export limit, and the rest is curtailed. Import beyond the import limit is recorded as unserved demand rather than silently supplied. Emissions follow a grid intensity profile, so a sustainability assessment is the same run. Place exactly one per site: it is the slack that closes the energy balance. No ports: this is a continuous asset. A demand charge on the peak import power is billed once at the end of the run.

parameters.name: import_profile
parameters.label: Import tariff
parameters.help: Import price by hour of the day, EUR/kWh. A flat tariff is a one-value profile.

parameters.name: export_price
parameters.label: Export price
parameters.help: Paid for every exported kWh: it enters Total Cost as a negative cost.

parameters.name: intensity_profile
parameters.label: Grid carbon intensity
parameters.help: kg CO2e per imported kWh, by hour of the day. It drives Total Impact, which is deliberately generic: use it for water, waste or any other per-unit impact instead.

parameters.name: import_limit_kw
parameters.label: Import limit
parameters.help: Connection capacity. Demand beyond it is recorded as unserved energy, not supplied.

parameters.name: export_limit_kw
parameters.label: Export limit
parameters.help: Largest power the meter may export. Surplus beyond it is curtailed, which the curtailment flow accounts for.

parameters.name: demand_charge_per_kw
parameters.label: Demand charge
parameters.help: Billed once on the highest import power the site actually HELD (the import flow's Peak Rate), the way a network operator bills capacity. 0 for an energy-only tariff.

info.title: Depot: PV, EV charging and heat pump
info.description: A depot on one electricity bus: a PV roof, the building's own load, twenty EV charge points and a heat-pump water tank, with a grid connection closing the balance. Nothing is wired -- the five assets meet on the named flow tags FLOWSUM() adds up, and the tank adds a SECOND medium (heat) fed from the same bus through its COP. Base unit hours, one week.
info.author: Naga
info.notes: EV charging is an AGGREGATE model: one level holds the energy still owed to the vehicles plugged in, so the peak it reports is a fleet average rather than twenty cars starting at once. The scenarios are the two dispatch questions a depot actually has -- shift the charging, or size the heat store -- and the unserved-energy KPI is what keeps smart charging honest.
